standard_prerequisites.use: The reduction uses the definition of a g^r_d as an equivalence class of pairs (L, V) from Definition definition-linear-series.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 612-617): if a proper scheme X of dimension <= 1 over a field k has a g^r_d, then X has a g^s_d for all 0 <= s <= r.

Reduction (proof lines 619-623): the claim reduces to the elementary fact that a k-vector space V of dimension r + 1 has a linear subspace of dimension s + 1 for all 0 <= s <= r; via Definition definition-linear-series a g^r_d is represented by a pair (L, V) with dim_k V = r + 1, and replacing V by such a subspace V' gives a representative (L, V') of a g^s_d with the same degree d.
proof_roadmap: Unfold the definition of a g^r_d as a class of pairs (L, V).
Shrink V to a subspace of dimension s + 1.
The pair with the shrunken subspace represents the desired g^s_d.
difficulty_reason: Lower-linear-series existence lemma (statement 612-617, proof 619-623): from a g^r_d one obtains g^s_d for all s <= r - the proof reduces to the elementary subspace fact (a vector space of dimension r+1 has subspaces of dimension s+1); combined with the unfolding of Definition definition-linear-series the argument is complete, no step omitted. H3: definitional reduction plus elementary linear algebra.
